messages.subject: stand-alone c++ example
parts:
Hi,

I'm working towards a python wrapper (using cython). I was wondering if
there's an example of a simulation written in c++ using only the c++ api
(i.e., without any intermediate call to an executable like stanc)?

Thanks,

Allen

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stand-alone c++ example
parts:
On 5/19/13 10:20 PM, a...@ariddell.org wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'm working towards a python wrapper (using cython). I was wondering if
> there's an example of a simulation written in c++ using only the c++ api
> (i.e., without any intermediate call to an executable like stanc)?

I'm afraid the only example of such a thing is the code generated
by stanc for a model :-)

The model class geneated by stanc handles a number of issues that
are hard to deal with directly, particularly the I/O of

-- data

-- initial values (requires transform to unconstrained)

-- parameter values (requires transform to constrained)

-- parameter names

-- samples

The constrained variable declarations get compiled to transforms
that include the differentiable log Jacobian determinant in the
overall log probability function.

The way we wrapped in R was to have the code compile a model class,
then compile it and dynamically link it. What corresponds to the
main() in the ordinary bin/stanc output is not used and instead,
the class is controlled from R to interface with its memory.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stand-alone c++ example
parts:
On 5/20/13 11:03 AM, Allen Riddell wrote:
> Dear Bob,
>
> Thanks. This makes sense.
>
> The challenge seems to be the platform-agnostic run-time compilation. I'm not
> familiar with any existing python library wrappers that do this (although I'm
> sure they exist). I'll look into the rstan code and see how it gets done with R.

R does have standard tools for both compiling binary
libraries and on-the-fly C++ compilation.

It looks like the weave sub-package of scipy supplies similar
functionality to the inline package we use in R. All of
our other compilation is done ahead of time.

An alternative to a deep integration is having the
compilation done by system calls. Our own makefiles
are tested cross-platform.

- Bob
